account:
Today has mostly followed my appointment schedule: morning office business, a grain inspection at the mill, lunch at home, an unsuccessful search for council letters, and afternoon tea with my neighbour. The mill stall had 74 hay bales, so I saw no evident grain shortage. No council letters have arrived, according to the secretary; the office chest contained schedule books rather than correspondence.

The unusual feature is persistent, vague gossip about a bridge or port change. Several townsfolk mentioned the bakery, naming the baker, innkeeper, freight and neighbour as people present. Someone reported the baker carrying a sack of bread. None of that establishes an actual change to a crossing. My neighbour says there is no definite information and has discouraged repeating rumours as facts. The secretary reports that freight and builder have no firsthand evidence either. I do not know whether the gossip reflects any real project or simply repeated misunderstanding.

There is also an evening gathering that deserves clarification. I knew of the approved 18:00 great hall lighting inspection with builder and secretary, and neighbour says builder has the lighting ready. Now innkeeper says he is here for our booked meeting and the inspection, and secretary mentions a 17:30 gathering. That gathering was not in the appointment books I read this morning. It might be an ordinary arrangement connected to the inspection, but I do not yet know its purpose or who arranged it. Builder is nearby, and innkeeper and secretary are with me in town hall. My best grounded expectation is that people are assembling for hall business and the lighting inspection; I have no evidence of a secret undertaking, nor grounds to connect the gathering to the crossing rumours.
